concern: Line 495 makes a_ce = i_ce && !g_v && !m_busy and line 504 uses it as the stage's enable; the route-table write (lines 148-150, enable at line 290) now needs it, while in the parent (parent.sv line 280) it used the plain global enable. o_stall is high then, but in the parent route writes never had to wait. Simulation: multicast to port 0 with port 0 not ready; route entry 4 = 0x06 written for one cycle; it stayed 0, and a later packet routed through entry 4 reached no ports and raised neither done nor miss. Also the 32-bit route value is cut to its low 8 bits and used as a port mask.

label: wrong
reason: The added flow cache works (it never changed an answer in testing), but like its parent the table silently drops any rule update that arrives while a search is running, so the update is lost and later lookups miss.
concern: design.sv lines 392-399 (parent.sv lines 171-178): rule writes are stored only when !busy, and the port list (lines 259-281) has no write-ready or busy output, so the writer is never told to wait. Simulated on both this design and parent 95c7ac4c1989: install rule 3 (key 0x11), look up 0x11, then send a write of rule 1 (key 0x22) while busy=1 -> valid[1] stays 0 and the later lookup of 0x22 misses. Closest call checked: the cache step itself matched a full search on about 2,050 random lookups with 416 evictions, 0 mismatches.

label: wrong
reason: The new 'ready for a lookup' signal stays on while the table is busy searching, so a lookup sent when it says ready is silently dropped, and rule updates sent mid-search are still lost as in its parent.
concern: design.sv lines 121-129: lk_ready = room && !halted counts the busy table as one reserved slot but does not wait for it to finish; the table (lines 278-286) ignores req and wr_en while busy; wr_en goes straight to the table (line 467). Simulated: rule 2 installed, two lookups sent back to back, each while lookup_ready=1; the second arrives while busy=1 and never gets an answer (2 handshakes, 1 response). Parent 199ba5664df4 (parent.sv lines 66-80, top ports 201-206 have no ready): simulated a lookup plus a rule write sent mid-search -> 1 answer for 2 lookups and the rule never stored.

label: good
reason: A real front-end scheduler with waiting lines and ready signals for lookups and rule updates, numbered replies and merging of repeat updates, which stops the parent from losing work sent during a search; its key fact ties the scheduler's 'request outstanding' flag to the table being busy or answering.
concern: Closest call: two watch-only counters (queue high-water mark, miss count) and three of the four new facts are plain bounds. Random simulation with senders that wait for ready and random clock-enable gaps: 406 lookups accepted = 406 answered in tag order, all 479 accepted rule writes landed in the table (76 merged), nothing handed to the table while busy. A rule write can overtake an earlier-queued lookup, which is normal for control updates.

label: weak
reason: It cuts the 12-step countdown into a 7-step part and a saved 4-step part kept in a new 'tail' register, so the output is high for exactly the same 12 steps as before; it is only a small split.
concern: Closest call was wrong (timing changed): traced by hand from one pulse, parent and child both keep irq_out high for 12 enabled steps and 'held' ends at 12, because the hand-over step (lines 30-33) still counts one step; old behaviour is intact.

label: wrong
reason: Keeps the parent's encoder mistake, and its new 'lock' gate quietly throws away the start and end marks of frames the old design sent (until it has seen four commas in a row, and again after 16 data bytes between frames), so those frames' bytes go out loose; in a random run it let through 0 of 196 frames.
concern: Own step: line 220 'do_sof = sof_req && o_sof_ok'; o_sof_ok is set only by a comma once lock_next holds (lines 27, 69) or by an EOF while locked (line 75); the sender is never held, a refused SOF is only counted (line 73), and the frame's EOF is then ignored (line 221, phase never reached PKT). Scenario: reset, comma, SOF, 3 data bytes, EOF: parent sends C S d d d E (1 packet), child sends C d d d (0 packets, sof_rej=1). Lock is also dropped after 16 data bytes between frames (lines 34, 53-57): frame, 16 data bytes, frame -> second frame's marks lost. 6000 random cycles: parent 196 packets, child 0. A 'lock' on the sender's own commas is not a real transmit-side feature either. Inherited: same enc4 table (lines 174-188) and select (line 214); simulated sweep gives the same 6 wrong codes, e.g. 0xF1 after reset -> 1000111110.

label: wrong
reason: Keeps the parent's encoder mistake, and its new guard quietly drops any frame that starts within 3 symbols of the last one ending, and cuts frames longer than 48 bytes with an ordinary end mark, losing byte 49, sending the rest loose and hiding the cut from the receiver.
concern: Own step: line 251 adds '&& pg_sof_ok' (holdoff==0, line 51; holdoff set to 3 on every close, lines 68-69) with no wait signal to the sender; lines 255-256 and 312-317 put the normal EOF symbol in place of the 49th byte, then the leftover bytes go out outside a frame and the real EOF is ignored (line 252). Scenario A: 4 commas, SOF, 4 data, EOF, SOF, 4 data, EOF: parent C S dddd E S dddd E (2 packets), child C S dddd E dddd (1 packet). Scenario B: one 66-byte frame: child sends 48 bytes, E, 17 loose bytes, drops 1 byte and counts it as a normal packet. 6000 random cycles: 171 vs 196 packets. Inherited: same enc4 table (lines 198-212) and select (line 238); simulated sweep gives the same 6 wrong codes.

label: wrong
reason: Keeps the parent's encoder mistake, and its new 63-byte limit also changes old behaviour: for a longer frame it swallows the next symbol (even a comma) to put an abort mark there, sends the rest of the frame loose and throws away the frame's own end mark.
concern: Own step is the closest call (a length limit ended with an abort mark, like PCIe's 'end bad' symbol, is a real feature): line 235 'do_abort = i_ce && frm_abort' and lines 264-268 replace whatever symbol is offered after byte 64 (data, comma or EOF) with K30.7, and line 229 then ignores the real EOF because phase is back to ALIGN. Scenario: 4 commas, SOF, 66 bytes, EOF: parent sends all 66 and E (1 packet), child sends 64, A, 1 loose byte, no E (0 packets). With a comma right after byte 64 the comma is lost (parent ...C d E, child ...A d). Matches the parent on 6000 random cycles (no frame over 63 bytes there). Inherited: same enc4 table (lines 183-197) and select (line 223); simulated sweep gives the same 6 wrong codes.

label: good
reason: Adds a real 4-entry frame log (frame number, finished or aborted, pixel checksum) that software retires with an acknowledge command; it never changes the old outputs, and its facts tie the pointers to the count and the newest record's frame number to the frame counter.
concern: Closest call: when the log is full a new frame overwrites the oldest unread record (lines 209-213), but the loss is counted in o_hist_drops, a normal policy for a history log; random tests against a reference list (108 and 96 frames, 66 overwrites) found no mismatch, every overwrite counted, and no unfinished record ever retired (the pin rule on line 114 holds).

label: wrong
reason: 'Done' now turns on when the last pixel leaves the new queue, but by then the next frame may already be armed and running, so 'done' stays on while the next frame is still being drawn and no longer means 'this frame is finished'.
concern: Lines 207-212 let arm_req leave FIN (clearing done) while the queue still holds the frame's last pixels, and line 224 sets done when the end-of-frame pixel pops whatever the phase; with arm_req and start_req kept on, frame 1 is generated by cycle 374, frame 2 starts at 376, frame 1's last pixel leaves at 389 and done stays 1 for nearly all of frame 2 (2,523 of 3,000 cycles with done=1 outside FIN, versus 0 for the parent on the same inputs); the parent fact 'done implies FIN' had to be dropped and the new facts are only bounds.

label: wrong
reason: The new 8-slot frame record queue only empties on cycles when no symbol is sent, so on a link that sends a symbol every cycle it fills after 8 frames and from then on every new frame start is refused and that frame goes out without framing, which the parent never did.
concern: design.sv line 305: q_pop needs !i_ce, so the queue drains only on cycles with no symbol; line 270: do_sof needs q_room (line 164) and line 271 only counts the refusal. Scenario: i_ce=1 every cycle, one comma, then 12 frames of SOF + 4 data + EOF: the queue reaches 8 with 0 records handed out, frames 9-12 lose their SOF (their bytes go out unframed, their EOF is ignored); o_pkt_cnt 8 vs parent 12, old outputs differ on 63 cycles (simulated). With one idle cycle after each symbol it matches the parent exactly. A sender watching o_q_full can only go on by stopping the line. Also weak traits: 8 slots copied by hand, a parity check that can never fail.

label: wrong
reason: It keeps its parent's flaw of throwing away a frame start that arrives right after the previous frame ends (now only counted), so a normal back-to-back frame goes out without framing, and the new second channel adds another rule that refuses its fifth frame if no channel-1 comma was sent.
concern: parent.sv (396217e14456) line 251: do_sof needs pg_sof_ok (line 51 holdoff==0; line 69 sets holdoff=3 at every frame end), so a start inside the gap is silently ignored; the starting design accepted it. The child keeps this at design.sv line 288, copies it to channel 1 at line 291, and only counts it (ifg_defer, line 312). Scenario: comma, SOF, 4 data, EOF, SOF, 4 data, EOF with a symbol every cycle: starting design frames 2, parent and child frame 1 (second frame's bytes go out unframed, its EOF is ignored; simulated). New in this step: lines 423-424 drop channel 1 to idle after 4 frames without a channel-1 comma, so its 5th SOF is refused (simulated: 5 sent, 4 framed).

label: wrong
reason: It keeps its parent's flaw: the queue of frame records only empties on cycles when the enable input i_ce is off, so with i_ce always on (which the grandparent handled fine) every frame after the 8th is refused for good, and the new 12-byte header lane makes the queue empty about three times slower, so it refuses frames the parent would have accepted.
concern: Inherited (parent.sv lines 270 and 305, same as design.sv lines 329 and 364): a start of frame is only accepted when the queue has room (do_sof needs q_room), and the queue only empties when i_ce is low (q_pop needs !i_ce). Scenario, simulated: hold i_ce=1, send a comma, then 12 frames (start, 2 data bytes, end). The grandparent sends 12 frames; the parent and the child send 8 and refuse 4. Each refused frame goes out as 2 bare data bytes with no start or end marker, the host gets 0 frame records, and 500 more idle cycles with i_ce=1 change nothing; it only recovers once i_ce goes low. Child's own step (design.sv line 364 adds && !hs_busy; the lane loads hs_left <= rd_hcnt at line 1110 and counts down one per cycle at line 1126): records now leave at most one per 13 cycles instead of one per 4. Scenario, simulated: 4 bursts of 8 frames with 12 data bytes each, each burst followed by 32 cycles with i_ce=0. The parent refuses 0 of 32 frames; the child refuses 15 of 32, and its line output differs from the parent's from cycle 193 on. What is fine: in a random run of 697 frames every header byte, header count and header XOR matched what was sent, in order, with nothing lost or extra (a copy broken on purpose was caught). Facts tie each slot's header count to the frame length stored in that slot, but say nothing about the header bytes themselves.

label: weak
reason: Adds a 4-slot queue in front of the second pattern check, but the queue is emptied every cycle, so it never holds more than one beat while the trigger is working and only adds one cycle of delay.
concern: Random runs of 15,000 cycles: at most 1 beat in the queue while the trigger runs. It fills to 4 only after 'done', with beats that a clear throws away. 'done' matches the parent one cycle later. The only misses (5 of 212 runs) are a clear arriving on that exact cycle, a side effect of the delay, so not counted as wrong. The stop pattern is now compared one cycle later (line 52), so rewriting it in the same cycle as a beat uses the new value.

label: wrong
reason: Six power-down sequencers share 3 'you may switch now' credits and the credit counting is exact, but the grant always favours the lowest-numbered domain, so domains 0-2 can lock domains 3-5 out forever just by asking again after each window.
concern: Lines 115-120 give the credit to the lowest-numbered idle requester; a domain that finishes (line 126) is idle and asking again the very next cycle (lines 104-109), so it takes back the credit it just returned. Scenario: hold all six req bits and all ce bits high; in 15,000 simulated cycles domains 0, 1, 2 got 750 windows each and domains 3, 4, 5 got none. Under heavy random asking (higher domains re-ask half the time) domain 5 got 6 windows against 605 for domain 0 and once waited 6,761 cycles. Credits are never lost: pool plus open windows always equalled 3 in every run. If fixed priority is judged acceptable here, the rest of the step (real switching budget, real credit-conservation fact) would be good.
second_reviewer_reason: Lines 115-120 always give the free credit to the lowest-numbered domain that is asking, and a domain whose window just closed (line 126) can ask again the very next cycle (lines 104-109), so in a 15,000-cycle simulation with every req and ce bit held high domains 0, 1 and 2 got 750 windows each while domains 3, 4 and 5 got none and waited the whole run (the same happened when domains 3-5 asked just once and kept asking), even though the credit count itself was always exact.

label: wrong
reason: Joining the checker to the frame-sync block pauses the checker whenever the one-slot verdict buffer is full, but the sender is never told, so accesses sent during the pause are silently ignored and the grant output stays stuck on an old answer.
concern: Line 191 (a_ce = ce && !rst && (!slot_vld || fs_en)) stops the checker and line 193 accepts an access only while a_ce is high, yet the top has no ready output (ports, lines 168-173). Simulated with fs_en low: of three one-cycle legal accesses sent 4 cycles apart, only 1 is accepted, and the other 2 never get a grant or a fault, even after fs_en rises (the old checker answers all 3). With legal, legal, illegal sent back to back, at the cycle where the old checker reports the fault this design still shows grant=1, and keeps showing it. Using access verdicts as 'good frame header' also makes little hardware sense.

label: weak
reason: Only adds a second property (the number field inside the output word equals the counter minus one); the hardware is exactly the same tiny table reader as its parent.
concern: Checked the new property and fact (out_q bits 63:48 against rd_ptr, lines 68-70): true and about the stored output word, but nothing was built; outputs identical to the parent on 6000 random cycles.

label: weak
reason: Joins the trigger to a brown-out filter by feeding the trigger's 'done' into a circuit meant for a low-voltage alarm, which makes little hardware sense, and its new counter qual_cnt counts exactly like the filter's own streak counter that the property compares it with.
concern: Closest call: there is no data path, so nothing can be lost or stuck. The proven fact qual_cnt == streak_b shows the new counter (lines 248-252) is a copy of the filter's streak counter (lines 134-138).

label: wrong
reason: The added quarantine counts the legal accesses it blocks as new violations, so one bad access followed by normal back-to-back traffic locks the checker out forever, and it is on by default, so the old checker's answers change.
concern: Lines 39-40 restart the lock window on every denial, line 85 turns every access made during the window into a denial, lines 80-81 add each of those to the violation count, and line 45 sets a permanent lockout that nothing ever clears (there is no reset); the defaults on lines 29-30 switch it on. Simulated with range 0x1000-0x1FFF allowed: one read of 0x5000, then 12 back-to-back reads of 0x1000. The old checker grants all 12; this one grants none, sets esc=1, then also denies 5 later well-spaced legal reads, with fault stuck high. Even with the window set to 0 (config index 24), 8 bad reads in a row still lock it forever, because the 3-bit count passes every possible limit.

label: wrong
reason: Feeds the power sequencer's ramp counter into a DCT block as if it were sample data, and the one-word sample holder is overwritten on every ramp step whether or not the DCT took the previous sample, so samples are lost.
concern: Lines 234-236 load smp_q and set smp_vld on every ramp cycle (a_step, line 198) with no check that the old sample was taken and no way to pause the sequencer; the DCT only takes samples in its write phase (consume, line 199). Simulation with requests held: downstream always ready -> 1,495 of 3,200 samples overwritten before use (during the DCT's 25-cycle read phase); dn_rdy low -> 3,199 of 3,200 lost; random -> 1,911 of 3,040. Also xfer_cnt (lines 240-243) is a copy of the DCT's own write counter, and the new property just compares the two.

label: weak

label: weak

label: wrong
reason: Adds a fake 3-cycle wait before each table read (the table answers at once) and a pass counter that closes the window by itself after 16 passes, so the same inputs now give one word every 5 cycles and the stream stops even though stop was never pressed.
concern: Lines 90-97 wait 3 extra cycles per word and line 72 sends only when pf_vld is set; lines 79-82 clear win after pass 16; line 20 also puts the pass count into output bits 67:64, which were always 0. Scenario: start once, then 1000 enabled cycles with no stop: the parent gives 999 words and keeps going; this design gives 128 words, closes the window at cycle 640 and drops out_v (simulated).

label: wrong
reason: It keeps the parent's self-locking quarantine (blocked legal reads count as new violations until a permanent lockout) and adds a copy of it for writes that locks out after only four write denials.
concern: Lines 59-60, 116-117 and 131 still restart the read lock window and add to the violation count for every read the window blocks, and line 76 makes the lockout permanent. The new write side (lines 65-69, 120-121, 133) does the same, with a default limit of 3 (line 45). Simulated with the same inputs as the parent check: one bad read, then 12 back-to-back legal reads, gives 0 grants (old checker: 12) and esc=1 forever. It also changes old behaviour: write denials no longer use the old lock settings at config index 24.

label: wrong
reason: Joins the power pool to a random-number generator in a way that makes no sense: the generator is only ever told to reseed, using a predictable status word as its 'randomness', so it never produces a random number; it also keeps the parent's lock-out of domains 3-5.
concern: Line 370 drives the command as 'reseed' (2'b10) whenever the mailbox is full, so 'generate' (2'b11) is never issued and out_data (line 289) stays 0 forever; line 383 builds the 'entropy' from the constant 0x5A, the closing-domain bits and the credit count, fed in at line 389. Simulation, 6,000 cycles, two input mixes: 0 generate commands, generator output never changed, reseed words like 5a040000 / 5a080001; also 188 of 895 window-close events were dropped because the mailbox was still full (line 381). The pool (lines 1-232) is the parent's unchanged, so its starvation bug is carried over.

label: wrong
reason: Sends power-window reports into an error-check (CRC) unit without ever adding the check bits, so every single report is flagged as corrupted, and more than half of the reports are dropped while one is waiting; it also keeps the parent's lock-out of domains 3-5.
concern: Line 357 shifts zeros in behind the 8 report bits, so the checker's 8 'check' bits are always 0 and the result is never clean for a non-zero report (the new property on lines 376-378 even proves the zeros). Line 359 only captures a report when none is pending, so other window closes are lost. Simulation: 351 of 351 frames flagged as CRC errors and 542 of 895 close events dropped (random run: 184 of 184 flagged, 250 of 436 dropped). The pool (lines 1-232) is the parent's unchanged, so its starvation bug is carried over.

label: weak
reason: Makes the duplicate counter count in steps of two with a 'half done' flag; a small tweak with no new job, and the fact only links counts.
concern: Old outputs match the parent on 6000 random cycles except the debug word: line 81 now shows half_beat where bit 2 of the cycle count used to be (that field cut from 3 to 2 bits); treated as a cosmetic debug change, not a break.

label: weak
reason: It joins a breakpoint watcher and brown-out counter to a small multiplier that is fed the bottom 8 bits of two watch counters, a pairing no real chip would make, and its new job tracker is only a copy of the multiplier's own busy flag and countdown.
concern: Closest call: a capture request that comes while a job is already waiting is ignored (about 3,700 times per 20,000 simulated cycles), but the waiting flag is visible outside and nothing the sender supplied is lost; simulation showed the old outputs match the parent exactly, the hand-off to the multiplier happens exactly once per job, the tracker always equals the multiplier's busy flag and countdown, and all 3,054 products were correct.

label: wrong
reason: It pastes the parent in six times and keeps the parent's bug: every ramp cycle the power sequencer drops a new sample into a one-place holding spot without waiting for the last one to be taken, so samples are silently overwritten whenever the block downstream is busy.
concern: design.sv lines 247-252 (parent lines 234-239): when a_step fires while smp_vld=1 and consume (line 212) is 0, because the transform block is in its read sweep (b_phase=1) or dn_rdy is low, smp_q is overwritten and that sample is never delivered. Holding i_req[0] high with all dn_rdy high: copy 0 made 208 samples, delivered 120, overwrote 88 (simulated; the parent alone: 88 of 192). The new step itself: six pasted copies under a 4-credit budget with fixed priority (low-priority lanes starve under nonstop requests), the six results XORed into one output (line 375), and every fact repeated six times.

label: wrong
reason: Six copies of the parent checker each keep its self-locking quarantine, and the new credit pool gets a credit back only when an access is denied, so with normal traffic all credits are taken and never return.
concern: Each mpu_region_checker copy (lines 62-85, 136-141) still has the parent's bug: in simulation, lane 0 got one bad read and then 12 legal reads, and locked out forever (es0=1, 0 grants in 10 later legal reads). Own step: credits come back only on a denial (lines 219-225), so legal-only traffic on all lanes left pool=0 and busy_o=111111 even after 200 idle cycles. The credits also gate nothing (grant_o is wired straight through, line 252), and all six copies hold identical 24-range tables fed the same address.

label: weak
reason: Joins a table reader to a random-pattern error checker through a copy of the reader's word counter, but the bit fed to the checker is always 0, so the checker measures nothing; the combination makes no hardware sense.
concern: Line 307 XORs the copied pointer, count and half-step bits. These always cancel, because pointer = count + half-step (a proven fact), so the checker input (line 312) is stuck at 0: 6,894 checker cycles in simulation, never a 1. Nothing is lost or stuck, and the reader half behaves as before, so this is a nonsense combination (weak). The 18 Oct hand review called it wrong for this glue.

label: weak
reason: It adds a second 2-slot waiting area in front of the beat queue, but that queue is emptied every cycle while the matcher is working, so the new area only fills after the job is finished and its new 'start beat lost, go back to idle' path can never happen.
concern: Simulated 60,000 random cycles against the parent (hundreds of start, finish and clear rounds): the output was identical, the new area was never used before the finish, the abort path never fired, and beats are only dropped after the finish, which a clear throws away anyway; the parent's own queue just delays beats by one cycle, so no fault is inherited.

label: weak
reason: Six copies of the table reader sit behind a credit pool, but their 128-bit words are not wired to any output, so only the credit counting does real work and most facts are the parent's facts repeated six times.
concern: Closest call: the credit pool is correct. A grant starts a copy, a release stops it, and the proven sum fact keeps credits from being lost. Only one release is taken per cycle (lines 167-172), which is fine if a requester holds rel until held_o drops. The copies' out_q only reach internal wires (lines 183-188), and the top ports (lines 124-134) carry no data. That is unused logic rather than a handshake loss, so weak, not wrong.

label: wrong
reason: It pastes the parent in four times under a shared budget and keeps the parent's bugs: a 'window closed' report is thrown away if another report is still waiting, and every report goes out with blank check bits, so the checker marks every one as corrupt.
concern: design.sv lines 402-404 (parent lines 359-362) record a closing only when no report is pending, and nothing makes the windows wait: two sequencers asked one cycle apart close one cycle apart and the second closing is never reported (simulated on the parent and on copy 0 here). Lines 397-400 and 410 send the 8 report bits followed by 8 zero bits instead of a real CRC, so the checker (line 277) sets err on every frame (2 of 2 frames on the parent, 1 of 1 on copy 0, simulated). The new top layer is a sensible two-level budget (3 windows per group of 6, 4 chip-wide) but built as four pasted copies with every fact repeated four times.

label: weak
reason: It only adds two counters for jobs sent and jobs finished, whose difference just repeats the existing 'job in flight' flag, and the extra condition it adds to the finish check is always true, so nothing the design does changes.
concern: Simulated 40,000 random cycles against the parent: every output matched, sent minus finished always equalled the in-flight flag, and it still carries the parent's pointless pairing of watch counters with the multiplier.

label: weak
reason: It adds a shared limit of 8 run permits over four copies of the earlier six-reader pool, and the permit counting is correct, but the 24 copied readers' results go nowhere and most of the facts are the same few facts repeated for every copy.
concern: Closest call checked: lines 350-370 and 425 - a take (one pool per cycle, fixed order lines 355-358) always grants exactly one lane inside that pool because want needs en, local credit and an unheld requester, and a give always frees exactly one lane, so spool and the four local pools stay in step (proven fact spool + t0..t3 == 8); reset restores both levels. The top's only outputs are spool_o, ipool_o, busy_o (lines 432-434); every copy's route words, prefetch words, window and valid signals go only to wires used in facts (win_vec_o/vld_vec_o left open at lines 378, 389, 400, 411), so the outside cannot even see when a lane has finished and should give its permit back - a design weakness, not a freeze, since release is always accepted. Fixed order can keep pools 2-3 waiting while pools 0-1 hold all 8. Parent 883ad54cc3d3 checked: its 4-permit pool is correct (weak, words go nowhere), nothing inherited.

label: wrong
reason: This step makes the copied position's count update one step late while its other parts still update at once, so the copied position now shows counts that do not match it and the error checker fed from it gives different answers than the design before.
concern: design.sv line 307 (if (g_pend) g_cnt <= g_cnt + 4'd2) and line 309 (g_pend <= g_hb) hold back the +2 of g_cnt by one step while g_ptr and g_hb still move at once, and stg_o (line 327) and stg_bit (line 314, the checker's input) read g_cnt uncorrected. Scenario: reset, en=1, start for 1 cycle, 3 window cycles, ld for 1 cycle, then step every cycle: the old design shows {ptr,cnt}=4,4 then 6,6; the new one shows 4,2 then 6,4 (and 2,0 instead of 2,2), and stg_bit becomes 1 at ptr 6 and 2 where the old one was 0. Side-by-side simulation with the same 15,000 random inputs: stg_o differs on 5,234 cycles, o_errs on 14,936 (final error total 768 old vs 17 new), o_sync on 14,410, win_o on 6,918; route outputs unchanged. Scenario: write wr_addr 25 with wr_data 0x1300 (limit on, 1 credit, mode 1), arm, start (frame begins, credits 1->0), abort mid-frame, arm, start again. In simulation the design then stays ARMED with a held launch and 0 credits for about 2,800 cycles until the run ends, and extra starts only restart it; the parent with the same inputs finishes the frame, and without the abort the credit does come back. Only the watchdog (off by default), a new write to register 1, or reset gets it out. Smaller point: the new unit reuses all eight old register addresses and reads data bits 8-23 that the parent ignored, so old writes with nonzero high bits now change launch timing (with those bits zero the child matched the parent exactly over 45,000 random cycles).
